study type: Quasi-experimental intervention study (criteria-based audit with pre- and post-intervention comparison)
exposure: Introducing standard guidelines for diagnosis and management of obstructed labour
Mandatory review by specialist for cases assigned caesarean section
Re-training and supervision on use and interpretation of partograph
Strengthening team work between doctors, mid-wives and theatre staff
cohort: The study audited 260 deliveries during a baseline period and 250 deliveries during a follow-up period at a referral hospital.
finding: A criteria-based audit, combined with targeted interventions, significantly improved the diagnosis and management of obstructed labour and reduced adverse perinatal outcomes.
mod_finding: The implemented interventions led to a reduced time for caesarean section intervention from a median of 120 to 90 minutes.
